name: Clay World
summary: Stop-motion plasticine miniature set: soft gradient-built clay figures with fingerprints, warm studio light and 12 fps boil.
description: Everything looks hand-rolled from modelling clay and shot on a tabletop miniature set: characters are stacks of soft lumpy balls and sausages without any outlines, each lit by a warm top-left key light with inner ambient occlusion, a warm rim along the top edge, faint thumbprints and a broad soft specular. The ground is a set of flat clay sheets (meadow, soil, purple clay, ochre paths, sunken glossy ponds) with raised, bevelled edges and a lumpy hand-pressed surface. Animation steps at 12 fps and every frame is a slightly different 'boil' of the same model, which sells the stop-motion feel.
avoidFor: grim or horror games that need hard darkness
games with hundreds of distinct unit types

difficulty.why: Soft gradient shapes are forgiving, but to really look like plasticine every new figure needs a few iteration passes.

technique.resolution: Native resolution; sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screen px per world unit × 1.2), 3, 5) px per world unit; ground is baked in 256-unit chunks at up to 2.5 px per unit.
technique.summary: Every body part goes through one 'clay()' painter: flat fill, radial key-light gradient, a tiled fingerprint pattern, inner ambient occlusion and a warm rim light produced by blurred offset shadows of the shape's outside, then a broad tilted soft specular. Parts are stacked back-to-front and cast soft contact shadows onto parts already painted.
technique.linework: No outlines at all. The only 'lines' are pressed grooves: a dark furrow rgba(58,22,18,a) of width w (0.3–1.1 units, round caps) with a lighter lip rgba(255,240,220,0.75a) of width 0.5w drawn 0.55w lower.
technique.shading: Soft volumetric gradients per part: radial gradient from lighten(col,0.2) at the upper-left (-0.25rx, -0.5ry) through the base colour (stop 0.5) to darken(col,0.4) at radius 1.22R; inner AO with alpha 0.5 along the bottom, warm rim alpha 0.42 along the top.
technique.lighting: One warm studio key light from the top-left (ground light vector (-0.42, -0.907)); shadows drift to plum (#401a34) not black, highlights to warm white (#fffbf0). Carved faces and cores glow candle-yellow (#fff7c4 → #ffd458 → #ff8f22) with additive halos. A warm brown vignette frames the screen.
technique.texture: Tileable 192 px fingerprint tile (concentric thumbprint arcs + tool smears, dark line plus light line 0.9 px lower, alpha 0.07–0.1) on every part; ground uses a tileable lumpy height field (2 texels per unit) whose diagonal derivative lights the surface ±10–15%.

paletteRules: Saturated but slightly muted 'toy clay' colours; nothing neon, nothing pure black or pure white.
Shadows are always mixed toward plum (#401a34 / rgba(58,20,40)) and highlights toward warm white (#fffbf0); never shade with grey.
Ground sheets are mid-value (luminance ~35–65%) so the brighter, glossier characters pop in front of them.
Each enemy family has a two-tone scheme (e.g. purple top layer over cream body) so hordes read as clusters of colour.
Glowing elements use only the candle ramp #fff7c4 → #ffd458 → #ff8f22, added with 'lighter' compositing.
Roughly 60% ground greens/purples, 25% character colours, 15% warm accents (orange, gold, cream UI).

typography.role: Titles, HUD numbers, card names, damage numbers (rendered as extruded clay letters)
typography.css: font: 400 40px/1.1 'Chewy', 'Baloo 2', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #f07a24; text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #c85e1a, 0 4px 0 #a84a12, 0 5px 0 #8c3c0e, 0 9px 10px rgba(40,18,6,.45);

typography.role: Body text, labels, card descriptions, hints

background.summary: A tabletop of flat clay sheets. Several noise fields decide where soil, purple clay, sunken ponds and ochre paths lie on top of the meadow; per-pixel signed distance to each sheet edge gives a lit bevel on the inside and a soft cast shadow on the outside (ponds are inverted: a sunken, darker bank). A tileable lumpy height texture modulates every pixel, then decals are pressed into the clay.
layers: Meadow base: mix of #76a454 and #8cac5a by low-frequency noise, times a ±4.5% tint field.
Raised sheets in order soil #986c4a, purple #66507e, sunken pond #7ebad2, ochre path #d6a262 (top): bevel width 3.0 units, cast shadow width 3.4 units, light vector (-0.42, -0.907).
Lumpy surface modulation: colour × (1 + MOD × m), m = 1 meadow, 1.1 soil, 1 purple, 0.35 pond (smooth), 0.9 path.

Decals (10-unit jittered grid): modelling-tool grass imprints, rolled grass sprouts, 5-petal clay flowers, pebbles (meadow); pebbles, pink worms, twigs (soil); spiral imprints, pebbles, tiny mushrooms (purple); lily pads, ripple rings, glossy light reflections (pond); thumbprints and pebbles (path).
Per frame on top of the ground: additive warm light pool under the hero (34×18 units, alpha 0.16), pickup glows, temporary clay splats where enemies died, clay mounds where enemies rise.

characters.summary: Characters are assemblies of 10–25 clay primitives (ellipses, capsules, lumpy Catmull-Rom blobs, custom silhouettes) painted back to front with the clay() painter, each with its own contact shadow on the parts behind. Proportions are chunky toy proportions: big head (~60% of the height), tiny stubby limbs, googly eyes. The hero is ~21 units wide and ~33 tall; each animation frame is baked separately with a different random seed so lumps and fingerprints shift (boil).
rules: No outlines: silhouettes separate through value contrast, AO at the bottom of every part and the soft ground shadow.
Heads and key shapes get a strong glossy highlight (spec 0.55, gloss 0.7); limbs a weak one (spec 0.15–0.35).
Faces are either carved holes with candle glow, white clay eyeballs with glossy black pupils, or dark sockets pressed into the clay.
Details such as pumpkin ribs, cloth folds and wood grain are pressed grooves, never drawn lines.
Walk cycles are 4 frames + 1 idle frame stepping at 12 fps; whole sprites also squash/stretch 3–5% per step.
Mirror sprites for facing; the light still comes from the top-left in both directions because the mirror is baked from the same lit art (accepted cheat).

effects.name: Clay crumbs
effects.how: Hits and deaths spawn 3–18 small baked clay balls (2 × 1.85 units, enemy colours) that fly with gravity 300 and squash to 1.25 × 0.72 when they touch the ground.

effects.name: Splat
effects.how: Killed enemies leave a flat lumpy clay pancake (4.6 × 2.4 units plus 3 droplets) that pops in with outBack over 8% of its 1.7–2.2 s life and fades/flattens in the last 30%.

effects.name: Squash death
effects.how: Dying enemies scale x by 1 + 0.7k and y by 1 - 0.8k (k = outQuad over 0.55 of the death time) with a fading white-cream flash overlay (#fff8ec).

effects.name: Hit flash
effects.how: A cream-tinted copy of the sprite is drawn at alpha min(0.55, flash × 0.8) while the sprite squashes 16% wide / 15% flat, plus an additive soft white flash puff (6–9 units, 0.12 s).

effects.name: Candle glow
effects.how: Carved faces, lantern pickups and brute cores get an additive radial glow sprite (rgba(255,214,120,0.85) → rgba(255,140,40,0)) pulsing ±0.08–0.1 alpha on the 12 fps step.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A baked glossy cream seed (#f8e8be) with a soft tapered streak behind it (rgba(255,244,214,0.75) → 0 over 11.5 units); the seed flips in steps by scaling y with 0.6 + 0.4|cos|.

effects.name: Rise from the ground
effects.how: Spawning enemies appear inside a dark clay mound and are revealed row by row in 8 discrete steps (only the part above the feet line is drawn) with a 12% wobble.

effects.name: Dust puffs
effects.how: Dash and landing dust are soft beige radial blobs (rgba(236,214,182,0.9)) that grow 0.6 → 1.5× and fade over 0.25–0.6 s.

ui.summary: HUD elements are soft clay slabs: cream radial-gradient panels with inner top highlight, inner bottom shadow, a solid 5 px darker 'thickness' below and a soft drop shadow; irregular border radii so no panel is perfectly round; bars are pressed brown grooves with glossy pill fills; numbers are Chewy with stacked extruded text-shadows; a faint thumbprint (repeating radial gradient) sits in a panel corner.

motion: Everything steps at 12 fps: animation time is quantised with Math.floor(t * 12) / 12, even when the game runs at 60 fps.
Boil: each step adds hash-based jitter of ±1.75% scale x, ±1.5% scale y and ±0.02 rad rotation (enemies ±0.04 rad), plus every frame index is a separately seeded bake.
Hero: 1 idle + 4 walk frames; walk steps squash 1.04 × 0.96 on contact frames and stretch 0.98 × 1.03 on passing frames, lean 0.035 rad into the walk; idle breathes ±2.5% on a 6 fps step.
Small enemies: 4-frame waddle with ±0.07 rad rock and 1.1-unit hop on odd frames; brutes: 4-frame stomp with 1.2-unit lift and ±0.03 rad.
Floaters hover 5 units up and bob ±1.6 units, tilt up to 0.12 rad with horizontal speed, alpha 0.84.
CSS UI animations use steps() timing (steps(3) wobble on hurt, steps(5–6) pop-in) to stay on the stop-motion beat.
Hits squash, never shake the sprite; only big kills shake the camera (3 units).
do: Build every shape from the clay() painter: base, radial key light, fingerprints, inner AO, rim, soft spec.
Paint parts back to front so each part casts a soft contact shadow (offset ~0.45, 1.4 units) onto what is behind it.
Press details in as grooves (dark furrow + light lip below) instead of drawing lines.
Quantise all animation to 12 fps and re-bake each frame with a new seed for boil.
Keep the light from the top-left everywhere: sprites, ground bevels, pebbles, UI gradients.
Give every actor a soft plum-brown ground shadow (rgba(44,24,16,0.5) centre).
Use the candle glow ramp for anything magical or important so it reads instantly.
dont: Don't draw dark outlines or ink lines; it instantly turns the look into cartoon vector art.
Don't use hard cel-shading bands or pure black shadows; clay shading is always soft and plum-tinted.
Don't animate smoothly at 60 fps; tweened motion destroys the stop-motion feel.
Don't use perfect geometric circles for organic parts; use lumpy blobs (11 points, ±6–20% radius noise).
Don't add high-contrast noise or grain on top; texture must be subtle fingerprints and lumps.
Don't make highlights tiny and sharp (that reads as hard plastic or candy); clay specular is broad and soft, only heads get a small glossy dot.
Don't use neon or fully saturated colours; plasticine pigment is slightly chalky.
performance: All characters, props, pickups and particles are baked once into canvases at 3–5 px per world unit (the clay() painter with shadowBlur is far too expensive per frame); per frame only drawImage blits, a few additive glow sprites and the screen overlay remain. The ground is the hot spot: per-pixel SDF bevel plus height-texture lookup per 256-unit chunk, computed incrementally with a generator and cached. Fingerprint tile (192 px) and height texture (256×256) are built once at init.
